thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: multiple GPU OOMs detected in runtime-prefill on gpu-prod-west-2. Containers restarting (count=34 in last 12m). Root cause suspected: very large prefill windows from long-prompt jobs. thread_ts=3009812345
oncall-maria: I’m on it — paging SRE and runtime eng. Starting triage.
eng-raj: seeing OOMs with large prefill sequences ~>12k tokens. Example stack: `killed process 12345 (python) total-vm: 180000000kB`
sre-eli: oncall, please capture node IDs. If it's node-level flapping we may need temporary drain.
oncall-maria: nodes affected: gpu-node-07, gpu-node-09, gpu-node-12. Node flip observed (kubectl eviction on 07).
eng-raj: paste of recent container log:
```
[2026-03-17T03:08:12Z] runtime: prefill allocate 15.2GB -> attempting 24.5GB
[2026-03-17T03:08:12Z] cuda: out of memory (OOM)
[2026-03-17T03:08:12Z] container: terminated by OOMKilled
```
pm-emily: any customer-visible errors yet?
cs-lead: preliminary telemetry: 2.3% 502s for gen endpoint in us-west-2 in last 10m; two accounts (acct-85, acct-402) showing spike in failed requests.
sre-eli: mitigation proposal: 1) apply short-term prefill token cap at ingress (drop/trim >10k), 2) enable fallback routing to smaller model pool, 3) mark affected nodes as unschedulable and cordon.
eng-raj: can push a config hotpatch to runtime-ingress: set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=10000 and PREFILL_TRIM_STRATEGY=prefix-trim in next deploy. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/runtime-ingress PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=10000 --namespace=prod`
oncall-maria: doing env patch now. Will monitor.
ops-bot: deploy triggered by oncall-maria: kubectl patch applied (deploy/runtime-ingress).
eng-raj: also enabling model-fallback: route requests >8k tokens to quantized-small-v2 in the routing table. Pushing route change.
cs-lead: heads-up: customer acct-85 uses very long-context agent; we should notify CS and suggest temporary prompt truncation.
pm-emily: drafting customer note now — ETA 15m.
sre-eli: cordoning gpu-node-09 to stop restarts: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-09` then evict high mem pods gracefully. Doing it now.
oncall-maria: node-09 cordoned. Evictions started.
eng-raj: after PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS applied and fallback enabled, OOMs dropped from 1 every 15s to ~1 every 5m on remaining nodes. Latency improved slightly.
cs-lead: customer impact: acct-85 impacted ~8% of their requests during the 20m window before mitigation; acct-402 ~1.2%. No data exfiltration.
ops-bot: status update: mitigation in-progress, customer updates queued, SLO impact = degraded for gen endpoint (US-WEST-2).
sre-eli: next step — schedule rolling reboot of gpu-node-07 overnight, but avoid mass drain during traffic. Recommend increase dedicated pool for quantized-small-v2 by +4 replicas to absorb traffic.
eng-raj: scaling quantized-small-v2 now: `kubectl scale deployment quantized-small-v2 --replicas=8 -n prod`
oncall-maria: scaled. Watching error rate.
eng-raj: quick note — added an autoshed rule to runtime router: if prefill>11k then throttle to 10 tokens/sec at ingress.
pm-emily: customer note sent for acct-85 and acct-402. Templates reused with incident details and ETA for full resolution.
sre-eli: preparing a short post-incident checklist: collect prefills with token counts >8k, correlate with model/tenant, and create eval prompt to repro.
oncall-maria: handoff: I’m passing to day oncall @09:00 PDT — summary: PREFILL OOMs on gpu-prod-west-2 caused container restarts and 502s for small subset of customers; mitigations applied: PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS env, fallback routing to quantized-small-v2, node cordon, scaled fallback pool. Monitoring green but still watching for regressions.
eng-raj: logging action items: (1) long-term: enforce server-side prompt trimming and better preflight reject; (2) investigate KV cache pressure for long-prefills; (3) add guardrail to model router for token-length.
cs-lead: CS to follow up with impacted accounts with remediation steps and timeline.
ops-bot: incident state -> mitigated (partial). Will update to resolved after 4h stable.
sre-eli: tagging for postmortem and scheduling incident review. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
